solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the daughter sits within the word for demand

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a demand or requirement
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone insists that one daughter is definitely in need.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'One' stands outside the container and comes first; only the daughter goes into the word for demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb of emphatic agreement, a synonym for certainly or truly.

clue.text: Article about ancient city united Pacific island

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the article is read from its end

blocks.note: the indefinite article
Ur of the Chaldees, the crossword's favourite ancient city
standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A news article about an ancient city that was united with a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in the western Pacific Ocean, in Micronesia.

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
ample means large or generously proportioned

explanation.surface: Someone describes their former partner as rather a large specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or instance taken as representative, which is what an example is.

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
the A1, Britain's longest numbered road, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Welshman sets off along a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the great road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords read its 1 as I. Dai is a typical Welsh first name, a pet form of David.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai is the stock Welsh male name, so crosswords use it for any Welshman.

clue.text: Perhaps football's special in this place

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for special
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Football is said to be special around here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks football as just one example of a round object, and 's is short for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A football is a ball, a round solid, so it is an instance of a sphere.

clue.text: Large duck that lady doctor put in pool of water

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so the doctor goes within the pool

blocks.note: the pronoun for a woman already mentioned
a lake is a large body of standing water
standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A lady doctor drops a large duck into a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That lady' is a pronoun, not a title, and 'pool of water' is a body of water rather than a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck is a large, boldly marked duck; a sheldrake is properly its male.

clue.text: Henry and Alan's meat conforming to religious law

blocks.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Al is a short form of Alan

explanation.surface: Two men named Henry and Alan buy meat prepared under religious rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like it should give just H, but it gives the nickname HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal food, especially meat, is prepared in the manner prescribed by Islamic law.

clue.text: Soldier maybe in boxing arena delivering tirade

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it, so the soldier is surrounded by the arena

blocks.note: boxers fight in a ring
a soldier is a kind of ant; 'maybe' flags the example

explanation.surface: A soldier, perhaps, is in a boxing ring shouting angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is not a military one but a soldier ant, a caste with large jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranting means speaking at length in a loud, impassioned way, exactly what delivering a tirade involves.

clue.text: Therapeutic dog had food around four

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so the eating word wraps the number

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ate is the past tense of eat
the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A therapy dog has eaten four meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Curative means able to cure illness, so it is a synonym for therapeutic or healing.

clue.text: Evelyn half concealed unknown wild cat

indicators.note: with half of the name hidden from view, only the other half of its letters remains

blocks.note: the name taken as written
in algebra x is the unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A woman named Evelyn, half hidden, watches an unknown wild cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half, EVE, is concealed, leaving the last three letters of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat of northern forests with tufted ears and a short tail.

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word strikes off its opening letter

blocks.note: to equip is to supply or furnish

explanation.surface: Someone scratches their head trying to come up with a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Scratching one's head sounds like puzzling over something; here it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a witty remark, a brief joke made in passing.

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over and worked, so these letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: bud is short for buddy, a friend
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend has grown the perfect garden shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' fits the gardening picture, which hides that it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia, the butterfly bush, is a flowering garden shrub with long purple spikes.

clue.text: Somehow not mind following graduate game

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters arrive in some other order
following means coming after, so the rearranged words are sent second, behind the degree

blocks.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Somehow a graduate doesn't mind following a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places the rearranged letters after the degree, so BA comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

indicators.note: lying outside something means surrounding it, so the sad word wraps around the next

blocks.note: sad means unhappy
pre is the prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Someone was miserable outdoors before a broadcast went out.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to spread it widely, as seed is broadcast across a field.

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a duct is a tube or channel; the capital T and question mark suggest London's Underground

explanation.surface: A fruit expert travelling on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the expert above the tube. The Tube is London's Underground railway, a deliberate distraction here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit is used figuratively for a result or outcome, just as a product is the result of effort.

indicators.note: to be represented is to be shown in another form, so these letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: the name taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Graham was the representative for a county.
explanation.walkthrough: Armagh is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagh is a traditional county of Northern Ireland, which is part of the UK.

clue.text: On French island, fail to see weapon

blocks.note: to miss something is to fail to notice it
île is French for island

explanation.surface: On an island in France, someone fails to spot a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'On French island' means placed above it, so the failing word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile is a weapon launched or thrown at a target, such as a rocket or projectile.

clue.text: To change shape, fiancee regularly used strong drug

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to morph is to change form
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A shape-shifter's fiancee took a powerful drug from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is a powerful opiate painkiller, a strong narcotic drug derived from opium.

clue.text: Sort of bread with hole at back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so this short word is read from its end

blocks.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of loaf with a hole at the back of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at back' reads as a location, but 'back' turns the little word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow bread of Greek and Middle Eastern origin that opens into a pocket.

blocks.note: first meaning: to fire someone from a job
second meaning: a fortified white wine once imported from Spain, Falstaff's favourite

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as rejecting a sherry, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for firing an employee and an old name for dry sherry-type wine from Spain.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the boring tool is sent second, behind the councillor

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for councillor
an awl is a pointed tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A sycophant, a dull bore, trails after a local councillor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring thing' suggests something dull; it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and low to the ground, which is to crawl.

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: jus is a thin gravy of meat juices
the final letter

explanation.surface: A proper gravy goes with the roast at the end of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair or right, so a just outcome is a proper or fitting one.

clue.text: Late itinerant circling empty room in last station

indicators.note: an itinerant wanders from place to place, so these letters move about into a new order
an empty word has had its contents removed, leaving just its outside letters
circling something goes round it, so the rearranged letters surround what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A late-running traveller goes round an empty waiting room at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but two letters taken as written, placed straight after the emptied room inside the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the final stop on a railway or bus line, the station at the end of the route.

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: caviar is sturgeon roe, fish eggs

explanation.surface: A Greek personality has caviar announced at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet, and character means a written letter.

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a train is a railway vehicle

explanation.surface: Racing a small vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a verb about speed but is the noun meaning a breed or line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a breed or variety of animal or plant, a race in the sense of lineage.

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops an initial aitch, so that sound goes missing from the word
embracing something holds it in the arms, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: holy means sacred or religious
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A religious Londoner hugs an author out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the dialect of working-class East London, known for dropping the h at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Openly means done in public view without concealment, a synonym for publicly.
